subtitles.en: Canon-cited Revelation chapters (1, 4, 6) — the throne-vision opening + the throne-room + the seven seals

descriptions.en: Three canon-cited Revelation chapters from Codex Sinaiticus (the only 4th-c. uncial preserving Revelation; Vaticanus is incomplete) + P47 Chester Beatty III (~250 CE, the earliest substantial Revelation papyrus). Rev 1 (John on Patmos + the one-like-a-son-of-man among the seven lampstands); Rev 4 (the throne-room with 24 elders + 4 living creatures — massive cross-corpus to Ezek 1 + Dan 7 + Shi'ur Qomah); Rev 6 (the seven seals, the Four Horsemen, the cosmic-signs). The Raëlian canon engages Revelation chapters 1, 4, 6+ at length in *The New Revelations* — acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applied at each canon-citation site.

sourceCitation: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg, 4th c. CE) as primary uncial witness — Codex Vaticanus is incomplete for Revelation. Cross-collation against P47 (Chester Beatty III, ~250 CE; Dublin) as the earliest substantial Revelation papyrus. Critical apparatus: NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT/THGNT. Commentary references: Aune 1997-1998 WBC 52A-C; Beale 1999 NIGTC; Koester 2014 AB; Bauckham 1993 Theology of the Book of Revelation; Boxall 2006 BNTC; Mounce 1997 NICNT; Smalley 2005; Reddish 2001; Caird 1966 BNTC.
